# 🛰️ Awesome Agentic Capacity Planning [![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://awesome.re)

> A living map of research on the infrastructure demand of LLM agents

[🗺️ **Explore the interactive map**](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/) · [➕ **Add your paper**](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#suggest/new/paper) (no GitHub account needed) · [✏️ Suggest a change](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#suggest)

A curated, living list of papers on what LLM agents demand from infrastructure, organized along the chain **Workload → Trajectory → Resources → Capacity**, with the open problems no paper solves yet. Every entry is also placed on an interactive map and coded in three matrices (key result, contribution, limitation).

## How to read this list

Each link of the chain has its own section, split by what the work does: measure, predict, decide, model or reproduce. Within a part, the papers closest to capacity planning come first.

🟢 Published · 🔵 Major-lab preprint · 🟠 Preprint · 🟣 Workshop or report · ⭐ Core to the goal

**map ↗** opens the paper on the interactive map, with its full coding: key result, contribution and gap, limitation.

## Trajectory \(W→T\)

LLM and tool calls, durations, idle time, success

### Measure

- **[Copilot in the Wild](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00101)** 🔵 ⭐ Agentic Coding in the Wild: Characterizing GitHub Copilot Traces at Production Scale *(arXiv 2026)* — 13\.5 million sessions and 3.2 million GitHub Copilot users. · _Characterize_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p000)
- **[AI Agents That Matter](https://openreview.net/forum?id=Zy4uFzMviZ)** 🟢 *(TMLR 2024)* — Analyzes agent benchmarks and evaluation practices. · _Isolate factors_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p120)
- **[BATS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.17006)** 🟢 Budget-Aware Tool-Use Enables Effective Agent Scaling \(BATS\) *(COLM 2026)* — Shows the web-search agent its remaining tool budget \(Budget Tracker\), then adds planning and self-verification \(BATS\). · _Isolate factors_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p027)
- **[HAL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11977)** 🟢 Holistic Agent Leaderboard: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agent Evaluation \(HAL\) *(ICLR 2026)* — Standardized evaluation harness that distributes tasks over hundreds of VMs and logs every LLM call. · _Isolate factors_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p030)
- **[TraceLab](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30560)** 🔵 TraceLab: Characterizing Coding Agent Workloads for LLM Serving *(arXiv 2026)* — Normalizes 4,265 Claude Code and Codex sessions into requests, steps and tool calls, and splits time into generation, tools and human think time. · _Characterize_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p020)
- **[SWE-Effi](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.09853)** 🟠 SWE-Effi: Re-Evaluating Software AI Agent System Effectiveness Under Resource Constraints *(arXiv 2025)* — Re-ranks 15 scaffold–LLM pairs on 50 SWE-bench Verified issues by the accuracy obtained per budget of tokens, dollars, local CPU time and normalized inference time. · _Isolate factors_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p031)
- **[Scaffold Effect](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22585)** 🟠 The Scaffold Effect in Coding Agents: Harness Choice as a Hidden Variable in Coding-Agent Evaluation *(arXiv 2026)* — Full factorial design of 3 harnesses, 2 models and 50 Terminal-Bench Pro tasks. · _Isolate factors_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p028)
- **[Stop Comparing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23950)** 🟠 Stop Comparing LLM Agents Without Disclosing the Harness *(arXiv 2026)* — On success, the variance due to the harness is 7.8 times that due to the model, and the model ranking flips in 6 comparisons out of 9. · _Isolate factors_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p002)
- **[When Agents Disagree](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11619)** 🟠 When Agents Disagree With Themselves: Behavioral Consistency as an Uncertainty Signal for LLM Agents *(arXiv 2026)* — 8,000 runs on 4 models. · _Isolate factors_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p001)
- **[Feitelson \(book\)](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781139939690)** 🟢 Workload Modeling for Computer Systems Performance Evaluation \(Feitelson\) *(Cambridge University Press 2015)* — Methods for modeling a workload, including heavy-tailed distributions, locality of sampling and goodness-of-fit tests. · _Characterize_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p035)

### Predict

- **[Hermes](https://doi.org/10.1145/3803390)** 🟢 ⭐ Hermes: Efficient Serving of LLM Applications with Probabilistic Demand Modeling *(ACM TACO 2026)* — A probabilistic graph, learned from 1,000 runs per application, gives via Monte Carlo the distribution of the remaining time, tightened at each step. · _Model the sequence_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p040)
- **[AgenticCache](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.24039)** 🟢 AgenticCache: Cache-Driven Asynchronous Planning for Embodied AI Agents *(MLSys 2026)* — For simulated robots, takes the next action from a cache of frequent sequences and lets the LLM confirm or correct it in the background. · _Model the sequence_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p007)
- **[Dynamic Speculative Planning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.01920)** 🟢 Dynamic Speculative Agent Planning *(ICLR 2026)* — A cheap agent proposes steps that the target agent verifies in parallel, and a DistilBERT learned online chooses at each step how many to launch ahead. · _Learn a predictor_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p037)
- **[Interactive Spec. Planning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00079)** 🟢 Interactive Speculative Planning: Enhance Agent Efficiency through Co-design of System and User Interface *(ICLR 2025)* — A fast agent executes up to 4 steps ahead, which a slow agent verifies in parallel, and everything after the first disagreement is discarded. · _Speculate_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p038)
- **[MICE for CATs](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.615/)** 🟢 MICE for CATs: Model-Internal Confidence Estimation for Calibrating Agents with Tools *(NAACL 2025)* — Estimates an agent’s confidence in a tool call from the model’s internal layers, decoded via logit lens and then compared with the final output by a probabilistic classifier. · _Probe or self-estimate_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p117)
- **[Speculative Actions](https://openreview.net/forum?id=P0GOk5wslg)** 🟢 Speculative Actions: A Lossless Framework for Faster AI Agents *(ICLR 2026)* — Faster models predict an agent’s likely actions, which are executed in parallel and validated only if the prediction is correct. · _Speculate_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p118)
- **[How Do AI Agents Spend](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.22750)** 🔵 How Do AI Agents Spend Your Money? Analyzing and Predicting Token Consumption in Agentic Coding Tasks *(arXiv 2026)* — SWE-bench Verified with 8 models. · _Probe or self-estimate_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p005)
- **[Sherlock](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.00330)** 🔵 Sherlock: Reliable and Efficient Agentic Workflow Execution *(arXiv 2025)* — Places the verifiers of an agentic workflow with a topological policy derived from fault injections, chooses the verifier with a learned selector, and speculates downstream during verification. · _Speculate_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p032)
- **[Speculate While You Reason](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25816)** 🔵 Speculate While You Reason: Teaching Agents to Predict Their Next Tool Call via Joint Agent–Speculator RL *(arXiv 2026)* — The same model predicts its next tool call, tool and arguments, and launches it while it reasons. · _Probe or self-estimate_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p036)
- **[Act While Thinking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.18897)** 🟠 Act While Thinking: Accelerating LLM Agents via Pattern-Aware Speculative Tool Execution *(arXiv 2026)* — Learns from past traces which tool call follows which sequence of calls, and launches these calls ahead of time on free resources. · _Speculate_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p008)
- **[Automata from Agent Traces](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23670)** 🟠 Automata from Agent Traces: Failure and Next-Step Prediction *(arXiv 2026)* — Reduces an entire corpus of agent traces to a minimal finite automaton, used to predict the next step and failure. · _Model the sequence_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p121)
- **[When2Tool](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09252)** 🟠 LLM Agents Already Know When to Call Tools, Even Without Reasoning *(arXiv 2026)* — A linear probe on the hidden state of the prompt’s last token predicts, before any generation, whether the task requires a tool. · _Probe or self-estimate_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p039)
- **[Beat the Long Tail](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13841)** 🟢 Beat the Long Tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training *(MLSys 2026)* — In RL, a length class drawn from past rollouts of similar requests, revised according to the length produced, tunes the speculative decoding of each response. · _Learn a predictor_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p041)
- **[Don’t Stop Me Now](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.01035)** 🟢 Don’t Stop Me Now: Embedding Based Scheduling for LLMs *(ICLR 2025)* — Re-estimates the remaining length during generation from the model’s internal states, and schedules requests accordingly. · _Probe or self-estimate_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p009)
- **[Tax et al. \(process mining\)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.02130)** 🟢 Predictive Business Process Monitoring with LSTM Neural Networks \(Tax et al.\) *(CAiSE 2017)* — An LSTM predicts, from the prefix of a business-process case, the next activity and its delay, then unrolls until the end of the case. · _Learn a predictor_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p044)
- **[Verenich \(process mining\)](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3331449)** 🟢 Survey and Cross-benchmark Comparison of Remaining Time Prediction Methods in Business Process Monitoring \(Verenich et al.\) *(ACM TIST 2019)* — Review of 24 studies and benchmark of 16 methods that predict, at each event, the remaining time of a case, on 16 real logs. · _Learn a predictor_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p045)
- **[Progress Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.23274)** 🟠 Real-Time Progress Prediction in Reasoning Language Models *(arXiv 2025)* — Estimates during reasoning the fraction of the trace already written, via a probe on hidden states or via tags that the fine-tuned model writes after each paragraph. · _Probe or self-estimate_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p043)
- **[Proxy BERT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.08509)** 🟣 Efficient Interactive LLM Serving with Proxy Model-based Sequence Length Prediction *(AIOps Workshop 2024)* — A small model predicts, before generation, the response length of a large LLM, and the scheduler serves short responses first. · _Learn a predictor_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p006)

## Inference \(T→R\)

GPU and KV cache

### Measure

- **[Cost of Dynamic Reasoning](https://doi.org/10.1109/HPCA68181.2026.11408569)** 🟢 The Cost of Dynamic Reasoning: Demystifying AI Agents and Test-Time Scaling from an AI Infrastructure Perspective *(HPCA 2026)* — Measures latency, LLM calls, tokens, KV cache and GPU energy of five agent designs under different budgets, versus ShareGPT. · _Characterize_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p023)
- **[Agentic AI Workload Char.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26297)** 🔵 Agentic AI Workload Characteristics *(arXiv 2026)* — Correlates Claude Code trajectories in Harbor with vLLM traces, turn by turn, for two models and five benchmarks. · _Characterize_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p025)
- **[Aries](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29069)** 🔵 Rethinking AI Cloud Infrastructure for Agentic Serving Systems with the Aries Experimentation Framework *(arXiv 2026)* — Instruments serving, sandboxes and harnesses with events correlated per trajectory. · _Characterize_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p022)
- **[Measure Before You Manage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.31057)** 🟣 Measure Before You Manage: Evaluating Agent Working Memory in Coding Agents *(AgenticOS Workshop, NeurIPS 2026)* — Logs 1,350 in-context objects across 55 trajectories of a coding agent, then compares two semantic working-memory policies with FIFO, LRU-D and UC. · _Characterize_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p034)

### Predict

- **[AdaServe](https://doi.org/10.1145/3767295.3769315)** 🟢 AdaServe: Accelerating Multi-SLO LLM Serving with SLO-Customized Speculative Decoding *(ACM EuroSys 2026)* — Serves requests with heterogeneous SLOs by building for each one a speculative decoding tree adapted to its latency target, with a pipeline that speculates, selects, then verifies. · _Speculate_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p116)

### Decide

- **[Agentix](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi26/presentation/luo)** 🟢 ⭐ Agentix: An Efficient Serving Engine for LLM Agents as General Programs *(USENIX NSDI 2026)* — Schedules the LLM calls of agent programs according to the service each program has already received, without predicting anything, and swaps the KV cache to CPU RAM on preemption. · _Schedule and admit_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p046)
- **[AgentDiet](https://doi.org/10.1145/3797084)** 🟢 Reducing Cost of LLM Agents with Trajectory Reduction \(AgentDiet\) *(FSE 2026)* — After each step, a cheap LLM rewrites an earlier step of the trajectory to remove useless, redundant or stale information, while sparing the prefix cache. · _Keep or restore state_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p033)
- **[CachedAttention](https://www.usenix.org/conference/atc24/presentation/gao-bin-cost)** 🟢 Cost-Efficient Large Language Model Serving for Multi-turn Conversations with CachedAttention *(USENIX ATC 2024)* — Saves each conversation’s KV cache in an HBM, DRAM, SSD hierarchy and reloads it at the next turn, with retention and prefetching guided by the scheduler queue. · _Keep or restore state_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p072)
- **[Continuum](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02230)** 🟢 Continuum: Efficient and Robust Multi-Turn LLM Agent Scheduling with KV Cache Time-to-Live *(PVLDB 2027)* — Keeps an agent’s KV cache during a tool call, for a duration chosen from that tool’s past durations, and schedules FCFS at program level. · _Keep or restore state_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p070)
- **[Helium](https://doi.org/10.1145/3802046)** 🟢 Efficient LLM Serving for Agentic Workflows: A Data Systems Perspective *(ACM SIGMOD \(PACMMOD\) 2026)* — Helium models an agentic workflow as a query plan whose LLM calls are operators, with a proactive cache and cache-aware scheduling that reuse prompts, KV and results across calls. · _Schedule and admit_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p112)
- **[InferCept](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/abhyankar24a.html)** 🟢 InferCept: Efficient Intercept Support for Augmented Large Language Model Inference *(ICML 2024)* — During a tool call, chooses for each request whether to keep, discard or move the KV cache based on GPU memory waste over time. · _Keep or restore state_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p011)
- **[KVFlow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.07400)** 🔵 KVFlow: Efficient Prefix Caching for Accelerating LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows *(arXiv 2025)* — In a multi-agent workflow with a provided graph, propagates a distance in steps to each agent’s next execution, and uses it to evict or prefetch the KV of its fixed prompt. · _Keep or restore state_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p073)
- **[Beyond Prediction \(tail\)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18431)** 🟢 Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference *(ICML 2026)* — Replaces length prediction with a gamma priority fed by lightweight statistical signals, with cache-aware preemption. · _Schedule and admit_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p119)
- **[SuperInfer](https://openreview.net/forum?id=RuslSHdIHa)** 🟢 SuperInfer: SLO-Aware Rotary Scheduling and Memory Management for LLM Inference on Superchips *(MLSys 2026)* — On GH200 Superchips, a proactive SLO-aware scheduler rotates requests, and an engine moves the KV cache between GPU and CPU in duplex over NVLink-C2C. · _Schedule and admit_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p115)

### Model

- **[HeraSys](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22578)** 🟢 HeraSys: Collaborative Serving of Multiple LLM Workflows via Fine-Grained End-to-End Optimization *(ICML 2026)* — Serves several concurrent LLM workflows by merging identical nodes across requests and by finely scheduling batches and resources. · _Cost model_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p059)
- **[Efficient &amp; Scalable Agentic](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.19635)** 🟠 Efficient and Scalable Agentic AI with Heterogeneous Systems *(arXiv 2025)* — Per-task cost and latency model of an agent graph, set by the bottleneck resource, and placement of tasks on heterogeneous accelerators under SLA. · _Cost model_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p056)
- **[Harness Effect](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06906)** 🟠 The Harness Effect: How Orchestration Design Sets the Token Economics of Enterprise Agentic AI *(arXiv 2026)* — Sets up a cost model in which cumulative input becomes quadratic in the number of turns if the history is replayed, then evaluates a harness that attacks each of its terms. · _Cost model_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p029)
- **[Teola \(Ayo\)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.00326)** 🟢 Teola: Towards End-to-End Optimization of LLM-based Applications *(ACM ASPLOS 2025)* — Turns each request of an LLM application into a graph of primitives, rewrites this graph and schedules its nodes. · _Cost model_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p058)

### Reproduce

- **[XPerf](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20370)** 🔵 Benchmarking LLM Serving Systems for Agentic AI Workloads with XPerf *(arXiv 2026)* — Traces an agent application without modifying it, as a DAG of LLM and tool calls with token IDs, then replays it under a different load. · _Simulate, replay, transfer_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p103)
- **[Saving GPU Hours](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07447)** 🟠 Saving GPU Hours in LLM Inference System Development and Online Workloads with Simulation and DBMS-Inspired Cache Replacement Policies *(arXiv 2026)* — Survey of LLM inference systems centered on cache management, theoretical tools to bound performance, and simulation to analyze a system before building it. · _Simulate, replay, transfer_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p113)

## Tools and sandboxes \(T→R\)

CPU, memory, disk, sandbox

### Measure

- **[AgentSysBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15127)** 🔵 From LLM Inference to Agentic Workloads: Characterization and Implications for Serving Systems *(arXiv 2026)* — Instrumented testbed of 10 agent applications, with a per-operation trace and container and GPU telemetry, plus 24 h of production traces. · _Characterize_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p021)
- **[CPU-Centric Perspective](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.00739)** 🔵 Towards Understanding, Analyzing, and Optimizing Agentic AI Execution: A CPU-Centric Perspective *(arXiv 2025)* — Profiles five agents whose tools run on CPU, then proposes COMB, which overlaps CPU and GPU phases through micro-batches, and MAS, which schedules a mix of tool-using and pure-LLM requests. · _Characterize_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p024)
- **[Not All AI Agents Are Equal](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19947)** 🔵 Not All AI Agents Are Equal: Characterizing Resource and Performance Dynamics *(arXiv 2026)* — The same bash tool is disk-bound on BigCodeBench, CPU-bound on SWE-bench, and stays light on APPS. · _Characterize_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p003)
- **[PeakBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24509)** 🟠 PeakBench: Benchmarking Resource-Aware Tool Invocation in LLM Agents *(arXiv 2026)* — Benchmark of 300 workflows over about 1,200 MCP tools profiled for static and dynamic cost. · _Characterize_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p049)

### Decide

- **[TrEnv-X](https://doi.org/10.1145/3805475)** 🟢 TrEnv-X: Transparently Share Serverless Execution Environments Across Different Functions and Nodes *(ACM TOCS 2026)* — Shares serverless environments across functions and nodes, through reusable sandboxes and memory images in a CXL or RDMA pool. · _Keep or restore state_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p048)
- **[DSec \(DeepSeek\)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22978)** 🔵 DeepSeek Elastic Compute \(DSec\): A Sandbox Infrastructure for Effective Agentic Training at Scale *(arXiv 2026)* — DeepSeek’s production platform for agent training and evaluation sandboxes, with placement, lifecycle, shared memory and on-demand image loading. · _Keep or restore state_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p122)
- **[DeltaBox](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22781)** 🔵 DeltaBox: Scaling Stateful AI Agents with Millisecond-Level Sandbox Checkpoint/Rollback *(arXiv 2026)* — Checkpoint and restore of a sandbox in a few milliseconds, for agents that explore several branches. · _Keep or restore state_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p012)
- **[AgentZip](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11294)** 🟠 Memory Compression for High-Fanout Agent Sandboxes \(AgentZip\) *(arXiv 2026)* — Compresses agent sandbox memory page by page while sandboxes wait for the LLM, and prefetches pages before they are requested. · _Keep or restore state_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p068)
- **[Crab](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.28138)** 🟠 Crab: A Semantics-Aware Checkpoint/Restore Runtime for Agent Sandboxes *(arXiv 2026)* — To resume an agent after a failure, checkpoints its sandbox only when the turn has actually changed the state, during the next inference. · _Keep or restore state_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p067)
- **[SpecBox](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23933)** 🟠 SpecBox: Speculative Sandbox Scheduling for Efficient LLM Agent Serving *(arXiv 2026)* — Predicts the sandbox the agent will request, through keywords in the token stream and a first-order Markov chain, and pre-warms it during inference. · _Keep or restore state_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p071)
- **[FaasCache](https://doi.org/10.1145/3445814.3446757)** 🟢 FaasCache: Keeping Serverless Computing Alive with Greedy-Dual Caching *(ASPLOS 2021)* — Treats keep-alive of serverless containers as a cache, with a Greedy-Dual priority combining frequency, initialization cost and size, and eviction under memory pressure only. · _Keep or restore state_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p074)
- **[Hibernate Container](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10963)** 🟠 Hibernate Container: A Deflated Container Mode for Fast Startup and High-density Deployment in Serverless Computing *(arXiv 2023)* — Adds a hibernated state between warm container and cold start, in which the suspended process has its memory swapped out, then reloaded on wake-up. · _Keep or restore state_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p076)

### Model

- **[Workflow-Aware Model](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/cpe.7743)** 🟢 Workflow Aware Analytical Model to Predict Performance and Cost of Serverless Execution *(CCPE 2023)* — Analytical model that estimates the response time and cost of a serverless workflow, loops and parallel branches included, then searches for the best configuration under a budget. · _Cost model_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p057)

### Reproduce

- **[Jamshidi et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.02280)** 🟢 Transfer Learning for Performance Modeling of Configurable Systems: An Exploratory Analysis \(Jamshidi et al.\) *(IEEE/ACM ASE 2017)* — Empirical study of 36 environment changes \(hardware, workload, version\) on four configurable software systems, to see what transfers from a performance model. · _Simulate, replay, transfer_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p107)

## Orchestration \(T→R\)

Durable state, messages, sleep and wake-up

### Measure

- **[Agora \(Azure\)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04458)** 🔵 Architectural Implications of Agentic AI Workflows *(arXiv 2026)* — 24-h Azure trace. Schedulers, orchestrators and runners have distinct CPU profiles, and orchestrators gate every inference and every handoff between agents. · _Characterize_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p004)
- **[Substrate-Portable Execution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06128)** 🔵 Substrate-Portable Execution for Production LLM Workflows *(arXiv 2026)* — Compiles five Rufus LLM workflows from a single definition to three targets: in-process, durable \(SWF\) and batch \(Flink\). · _Isolate factors_ · [map ↗](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#papers/paper/p111)

### Measure

## Contributing

**Your paper, system, trace or benchmark belongs here?** Add it in two minutes, without a GitHub account:

1. Open [Add your paper](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/#suggest/new/paper) on the interactive map.
2. Fill in its card and, if you like, its place in a matrix and on the map.
3. Say why in one sentence and send. Your suggestion becomes a pull request; once the maintainer merges it, it appears in this list and on the site.

You can correct or complete any entry the same way, with **Suggest an edit** on its card, or leave a comment.

With a GitHub account, you can also edit [`data.json`](data.json) and open a pull request. This README is generated from `data.json`: do not edit it by hand.

**What fits:** research and systems on agent workloads and trajectories, the inference and tool resources agents use, the orchestration of long-running agents (state, messages, sleep and wake), and capacity planning (placement, sizing, SLOs), including traces, benchmarks and simulators.

## About this list

It started as a literature review on predicting the infrastructure demand of LLM agents. The [interactive map](https://hpmp-l.github.io/InteractiveMap/) shows how the papers connect, and its three matrices code every paper. How the site and its suggestion pipeline work: [DEVELOPING.md](DEVELOPING.md).
